greeting: Hi! I'm Bee Bot. Ask me about budgeting, needs vs wants, saving or the 50/30/20 rule. Try one of the suggested questions below!
fallback: Sorry, Bee can only answer questions about student budgeting, saving and spending. Try asking "What is a need?", "How much should I save?" or "How do I avoid overspending?".

rules.answer: Hello! What would you like to learn about money today?
The 50/30/20 rule splits your income: 50% for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings. Try it in the calculator.

A need is something you must pay for to live or study: rent, basic food, transport to class, required textbooks. A want is nice to have but optional, like milk tea or new clothes. Quick test: could you go without it for 24 hours without hurting your life or studies?
rules.linkLabel: Play the Needs vs Wants game

rules.answer: To avoid overspending: 1) set a weekly spending limit, 2) track every expense, 3) wait 72 hours before buying wants, 4) turn off shopping app notifications, 5) pay with a separate account that only holds your 'wants' money.
Set reminders 3 days before each bill is due, and review subscriptions every month: cancel anything you didn't use in the last 30 days.
A common guideline is to save 20% of your income (the 50/30/20 rule). If that's too much right now, start with 5-10% and increase it later. Save on the day you get money, before spending.
An emergency fund covers surprises like a broken phone or bike. A good first target for students is 3-5 million VND.
Be careful! Pay-later wallets and credit cards charge high late fees and can hurt your credit history. Only use them if you have a steady income to repay.
A budget is a plan for your money: list your income, then your fixed and variable expenses, and decide what to save.
Write down every expense, even 5,000 VND. The Expense Planner adds up your totals for you.
Try the 24-hour rule before buying, cook at home, and shop after 7 PM for discounted fresh food.
You can send feedback or contact the team on the Contact page.
BudgetBee is for learning only. It is not a bank and cannot move or store real money.
You're welcome! Keep buzzing toward your goals
Good part-time jobs for students: tutoring, café or shop shifts, freelance design or writing. Never pay a fee to get a job, that's a scam sign.
Never share your OTP or password, check the account name before paying by QR, and ignore "easy job, high pay" offers that ask for a deposit.
When eating out with friends, agree on how to split before ordering. If you lend money, note it down and agree on a return date.
Rent is a fixed need. Try to keep it under about 35-40% of your income, or share a room to cut costs.
Start a sinking fund: save a small amount every month so tuition and textbooks don't surprise you at the start of each semester.
Try the 30-day savings challenge: one small money habit a day.
Take the 5-question quiz in Budgeting Basics. Score 4 or more to earn the Worker Bee badge
There are several budgeting methods: 50/30/20, envelopes, zero-based and pay-yourself-first. Compare them to find your fit.
Check the Money glossary for simple definitions of words like compound interest, BNPL and CIC.
Got lucky money for Tết? Try splitting it: 50% savings, 30% for something you've planned, 20% to enjoy now.
